material_findings.citation: exec.rs:4475 `if !bgp_uses_binary(patterns) { return Ok(None) }` — function body NOT in packet
material_findings.finding: The entire oracle assumes eval_bgp_binary_capped is entered. A 2-pattern BGP sharing TWO variables (?s,?o) is exactly the shape a cyclicity/WCOJ gate might reject; if it returns false the query falls back to full evaluation and every declared count (2 builds/128 visits/1 scan) is void.
material_findings.required_resolution: Read bgp_uses_binary and its cyclicity helper on 4595388 before scheduling the witness; treat as path-blocking, not as a runtime surprise.

material_findings.citation: exec.rs:4512 `let reuse_rhs = !budget::active();` (budget module inline, not excerpted)
material_findings.finding: rhs_scan_closures=1 and the 'scan cache already used once' premise depend on QueryBudget::unlimited() being non-armed. Unproven in the packet.
material_findings.required_resolution: Read budget::active/with_budget; keep the oracle assertion on scan-closure count so a mismatch stops the run.

material_findings.citation: store.rs:36-38 BUILT; exec.rs:4588 merge test; lib.rs:864 algebra-rewrite arm; exec.rs:4300, 6607 zk
material_findings.finding: Path is configuration-fragile. Under compact-index/wasm BUILT={Spo,Pos,Osp} the seed's subject sort is unavailable, seed sorted_by becomes ?o, merge_var==rhs.sorted_by and the step is a MERGE with zero hash builds. algebra-rewrite could alter pattern order/filter placement; zk bypasses try_capped and pushdown.
material_findings.required_resolution: Gate the witness test on BUILT (as exec.rs:21739 already does) and on cfg(not(algebra-rewrite/zk/compact-index)), and assert the observed kernel, not only the bag.

material_findings.citation: exec.rs:8212 est; 8264 goo_seed min_by_key; store.rs:1166 estimate
material_findings.finding: Seed selection rests on 2048 vs 2049 — a one-triple margin. min_by_key returns the FIRST minimum, so any tie or overlay correction makes Q the seed and destroys the 'RHS is the small filtered side' construction.
material_findings.required_resolution: Pre-register a slightly wider filler margin AND an assertion on observed (seed, est pair) now; no post-mismatch tuning is permitted.

material_findings.citation: exec.rs:9073 smaller-side test; 4519-4525 block ends; 4439-4445 CAPPED_SEED_BLOCK/…_2
material_findings.finding: Value ceiling is structural, not incidental. RHS is the build side only when the running block exceeds RHS rows, so a reusable RHS table is bounded by the PREVIOUS block size (1024, then 65536); at most two builds can ever be skipped per query, and with >=3 patterns the running result size varies per block so the build-side choice (and hence reuse validity) can flip.
material_findings.required_resolution: Quantify the maximum reachable saving (rows and share of block time) before any implementation decision; this witness saves one 64-row build.

material_findings.citation: exec.rs:4645-4667 CAPPED_RHS_STORAGE/first-fit; 4720-4726 charge-or-scratch; retention-plan invalidation bullet 3
material_findings.finding: Regression risk against today's behaviour: hash charges compete first-fit for the same 4MiB, and a still-valid but never-reused table stays charged until query exit, so a query that currently reuses scans may stop doing so.
material_findings.required_resolution: Define priority/refund policy (refund on build-side flip or on a step that cannot use hash) or a hard sub-cap on the hash share, plus a control witness on a query where scan reuse currently fires.

material_findings.citation: exec.rs:4436-4438 first-block rationale; 4632-4637 satisfied/break; retention-plan hash_charge bullet 3
material_findings.finding: Charging at build time makes the O(entries) spill scan fall on first-block hits — precisely the ASK/LIMIT-1 case the capped chain exists to accelerate — with zero chance of reuse.
material_findings.required_resolution: Defer the charge/publication decision to the end of the block, after `satisfied` is computed: a first-block hit then never pays accounting. Evaluate this before implementing.

material_findings.finding: allocation_size is a snapshot of the current allocation (0 for the empty singleton, correct for empty partitions). Any post-publication mutation of a cached table would silently stale the charge.
material_findings.required_resolution: Freeze cached tables after charging (probe path is read-only via raw_entry); assert no insertion after publication.

material_findings.finding: key_cols order derives from build.vars filtered by probe membership; a changed probe var set silently changes the build key projection.
material_findings.required_resolution: Identity check must compare the ordered build-column descriptor derived the same way, with a test that a probe-var change forces a rebuild.

material_findings.finding: A parallel cached adapter duplicates hash_join_ref's side selection/layout logic and will drift.
material_findings.required_resolution: Prefer parameterising hash_join_ref with an optional prebuilt table slice over a second implementation.

witness_assessment: Derivation independently re-checked and it holds on the cited source, conditional on F1-F4. Confirmed: filter binds to pattern 0 (Q) at pos 2 (6613-6622); seed=P via est 2048<2049 (8264); seed sort col 0 (8270-8279) with Pso giving actual sorted_by ?s; blocks 0..1024 and 1024..2048 (4519-4525); connecting.len()==2 excludes bind (4549); scan_sort=Some(2) from the pushed filter overrides the merge candidate (4564); Pos gives rhs.sorted_by=?o so the merge test fails (4588); hash_join_ref picks RHS as build because 1024>64 with `<=` favouring LHS on ties (9073); both sides <50_000 so serial build+probe (9109-9121, 9148) => 2 builds, 128 visits; probe_only empty, out_vars=[?s,?o]; cap 65 > 64 so `satisfied` never fires and both blocks run irrespective of dictionary id order (4632); residual empty, so the bag is exactly 0..15 four times (64 rows), non-distinct projection. This is a work-count witness only: it is neither latency nor heap evidence, it exercises no spilled Key/Posting and no 64-partition build, and it requires a cfg(test) build-side observer that the existing scan observer (4507/4573) cannot substitute for. The negative control (drop only the hash before block 2, keep the scan entry) is well designed.
accounting_assessment: Plausible and within existing policy. allocation_size is safe and public in the pinned 0.17.1 (map.rs:2006 -> raw.rs:702 -> allocation_size_or_zero), returns the requested layout size, and yields 0 for unallocated partitions. Inline Key/Posting payloads live in the bucket array so charging allocation_size plus spilled capacities (Id/usize element sizes) double-counts nothing; tables Vec capacity and the enlarged Option<CappedRhs> slot capacity are charged, and capped_rhs_cache's checked arithmetic pattern (4649-4667) extends cleanly. Scope wording correctly excludes allocator rounding, transient build state and RSS/peak, so no unsupported allocator claim is made. Two caveats: retaining table A while building table B introduces a new coexistence of retained bytes (bounded by the same shared 4MiB, but the report should say so), and F7/F8 above.
semantic_boundaries: No boundary violation found in the design as written. Build-side choice is recomputed and reuse is gated on RHS-as-build with equality still selecting LHS, matching 9073. out_vars/probe_only/JoinKeys recomputed per invocation; only the ordered build-key projection is reused. Postings are usize indices into the retained rows, so the stated rule (drop tables with the rows, never hold two generations, refund before replacement) is necessary and sufficient — no self-referential borrow arises. Polling is untouched: builds carry no poll; hash_probe_serial polls per probe row (join.rs:406-412) and the parallel snapshot/fold/reduce/sticky check (9130-9144) is unchanged; serial-vs-partitioned selection is deterministic in build.rows.len(), so representation cannot flip for a fixed retained RHS. Output row order per block is identical to a rebuild (ascending postings, same rows). ZK stays out of reach because try_capped returns None when recording (4300) and split_sargable keeps filters residual (6607) — this holds only if the cache stays strictly inside eval_bgp_binary_capped.
evidence_still_needed: Source: bgp_uses_binary (+cyclicity helper), inline budget module (active/exhausted/cap_alloc), view::default_is_empty, dict::is_inline/INLINE_BASE/inline_pass_values, probe_key_eq, capped_rhs_tests harness, project_bindings.

Runtime (later): observed parsed pattern order and filter assignment, seed index and both estimates, kernel per step, build side, tables.len(), build-row visits, scan-closure count, exact bag, and the negative control.
Design answers before implementation: F5 value ceiling, F6 crowd-out control on a query where scan reuse currently fires, F7 deferred-charge variant.
Only afterwards: same-head bounded latency/heap evidence and spill/partition accounting fixtures.
recommended_next_step: Schedule nothing executable now: the observed reserve 2,016,718,848 B is below both the 2,214,592,512 start and the 2,147,483,648 continuous floor, so the proposed witness cannot lawfully begin under its own stop conditions. Next action is source-only: read F1/F2 functions on 4595388, and pre-register the cfg/BUILT gating (F3) and the widened estimate margin plus seed assertion (F4). If and only if those clear and stable free space with a confirmed warm profile appear, run the single 480s/256MiB/jobs1/offline instrumented witness plus its negative control, stopping on any path mismatch. Keep the reuse feature itself unapproved until F5-F7 are answered; on current reasoning the expected saving (at most two builds, each bounded by the preceding block size) is small relative to the accounting and crowd-out risk.
